newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ipea sees 1997 GDP growing 4.0-5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ipea sees 1997 GDP growing 4.0-5.0 pct.

text.p: Brazil's Applied Economic Research Institute (Ipea) forecasts the economy will grow between 4.0 and 5.0 percent in 1997, led by manufacturing and mineral extraction, Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said on Friday.
Ipea research director Claudio Considera told Gazeta that Brazil's gross domestic product grew an estimated 3.2 percent in 1996.
The estimates will be released today by Ipea in its monthly report for January, Gazeta said.

Considera also told the newspaper the country's GDP will grow 4.6 percent in the first half of this year. He sees a natural economic slowdown compared with the high growth rate of around 6.0 percent in the second half of 1996.
